title: 69 arrested under Arunachal anti-terror law after protests against dam project turn violent

ai.summary: Police arrested 69 people under Arunachal Pradesh's anti-terror law after violent protests against a proposed 12,500-megawatt dam project in Pasighat on Friday, with security forces deployed in the Siang Valley.

facts.claim: 69 persons have been arrested and four detained for their alleged role in the violence
facts.quote: Sixty-nine persons have been arrested and four detained for their alleged role in the violence that broke out on Friday in Arunachal Pradesh’s Pasighat during a protest against a proposed dam, Inspector General of Police Hibu Tamang told Scroll on Tuesday.

facts.claim: The dam project is a 12,500-megawatt power project on the Siang river
facts.quote: Several organisations have been protesting against the proposed 12,500-megawatt power project on the Siang river.

facts.claim: Protesters vandalised and set fire to an office of the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation and a police station in Pasighat
facts.quote: On Friday, protesters vandalised and set fire to an office of the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation and a police station in Pasighat after security personnel fired tear gas during the agitation.

facts.claim: The police filed 55 cases in connection with the violence
facts.quote: On Tuesday, Tamang told Scroll that the police had filed 55 cases in connection with the violence.

facts.claim: Arrests and detentions were made in Upper Siang, Siang and East Siang districts under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities Prevention Act
facts.quote: The arrests and detentions were made in Upper Siang, Siang and East Siang districts under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities Prevention Act.

facts.claim: Twenty-six criminal cases have been registered in Upper Siang, 21 in Siang and six in East Siang district
facts.quote: Twenty-six criminal cases have been registered in Upper Siang, 21 in Siang and six in East Siang district.

facts.claim: Additional forces deployed in the Siang Valley: 30 companies of CAPF and three companies of Assam Police
facts.quote: ‘Earlier, we had 21 companies of Central Armed Police Forces,’ said the police officer. ‘Now, nine more have come. A total of 30 companies of CAPF and three companies of Assam Police are deployed apart from the Arunachal Police personnel.'

ai.background_note: Protests against the Siang dam project, which would affect 27 villages, have led to police deploying paramilitary forces and filing multiple cases in Arunachal Pradesh.
